text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me your age and when you first noticed these skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the child experience any fever or general malaise before the lesions appeared? Have you noticed any lesions on the trunk or face that might help distinguish between molluscum contagiosum and varicella?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do the lesions appear to have a central dimple or umbilication, and have they spread to other areas like the face or groin? I would also like to examine the lesions closely to confirm their characteristic appearance. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, up-to-date immunizations, no significant illnesses. Social history: Attends daycare three times per week.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of pearly papules with central umbilication is classic for molluscum contagiosum, especially given the daycare exposure. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum Contagiosum
